# Crypto Lab — algorithm and exhibit catalog

<!-- catalog-sync:begin — generated by tools/catalog-sync.js from index.html cards and tools/catalog-exhibits.json source reviews; do not edit by hand -->

The algorithm facts below are generated from `index.html` cards. The card facts
are derived from each lab's own source by
`tools/catalog-evidence.js`, and each implemented algorithm carries the `file:line`
where the evidence is. Source shapes the scanner cannot establish are recorded
in `tools/catalog-reviewed.json` at a pinned lab commit. Specific UI actions and
outcomes come from the separate, source-pinned `tools/catalog-exhibits.json` review.
Nothing in this generated document is edited by hand.

**Implemented** means the lab's code computes it — the algorithm appears in a
declaration, an invocation, a module import, a WebCrypto call, or a pinned source review.
**Referenced** means the lab names it without implementing it: a lab that teaches an
attack on HQC by modelling its decode time references HQC without implementing HQC.
The distinction is the point of the index, and a grep cannot make it.

Regenerate with `node tools/catalog-sync.js`; re-derive the underlying facts with
`node tools/catalog-evidence.js write`; re-check every anchor against the lab clones
with `node tools/catalog-evidence.js verify`.
To extend a section entry, review the lab's current default branch and add
its named control, learner action, computed or displayed result, concepts,
execution status, limits, and source lines to `tools/catalog-exhibits.json`.
Pin the full source commit and set the scope to `selected` unless every
section was checked. Run `node tools/catalog-exhibits.js verify` against
available lab checkouts, then regenerate and check this catalog.

## Find a concept in an exhibit

Use this index to locate the exact learner action or explanation when assessing
a new paper, book, or standard. **Interactive** changes a live result;
**comparison** changes options and shows their differences; **explanation** is
text a learner can read, with no interactive implementation implied.
**Execution status** is separate: `real-crypto` runs cryptographic operations;
`real-operation` performs another actual computation (such as image encoding);
`simulation` models behavior; `real-values` visualizes sourced parameters;
`conceptual` walks through an idea without running its cryptographic internals.
A `related` term is context only, never proof that a concept is taught or implemented.
The implementation index farther down answers a different question.

The exhibit map currently records **182 sections in 36 of 243 labs**
(0 complete lab inventories, 36 selected-section reviews).
**PARTIALLY REVIEWED** means only selected sections were mapped: omission says
nothing about the remaining panels. Other labs are **NOT REVIEWED**. Inspect
their current source before ruling out a concept, including for partial maps.
For a reviewed lab, verify the pinned commit is still its current default branch
before relying on this index for a fresh assessment.

## Overlap report

Pairs of labs that implement the same algorithms, weighted so that sharing a rare
algorithm counts and sharing SHA-256 does not. An overlap is not a fault — two labs
may teach the same primitive from different angles — but an overlap **with no stated
difference** is a question nobody has answered, and a visitor choosing between the
two has nothing to go on.

82 pairs: 10 with a stated difference, **0 examined and found to be duplication**, 72 nobody has looked at.

A pair marked DUPLICATION is a finding, not a description: someone read both and
found no difference worth having. It is listed first because it is the only row here
that asks for a decision.

**HPKE Envelope / Blind Relay**

- **Shared:** ChaCha20, ChaCha20-Poly1305, DHKEM, HKDF, HPKE, Poly1305, SHA-256
- **Stated difference:** **none stated**

**SNARK Arena / Polynomial Forge**

- **Shared:** Groth16, KZG commitment
- **Stated difference:** **none stated**

**Frodo Vault / Scloud+ Vault**

- **Shared:** FrodoKEM, LWE, ML-KEM
- **Stated difference:** both are unstructured-LWE KEMs: frodo-vault is FrodoKEM, the conservative plain-LWE design that avoids algebraic structure outright; scloud-vault is Scloud+, which keeps unstructured LWE but adds ternary secrets and Barnes-Wall lattice coding for efficiency

**KDF Chain / KDF Arena**

- **Shared:** Argon2, HKDF, PBKDF2, scrypt, SHA-256
- **Stated difference:** kdf-chain teaches what problem each KDF solves and walks a decision tree for choosing one; kdf-arena benchmarks the same four side by side and reports attacker cost against wall-clock time

**Factor Forge / Residue Gate**

- **Shared:** Jacobi symbol, Miller–Rabin
- **Stated difference:** **none stated**

**FROST Threshold / Shamir vs FROST**

- **Shared:** Ed25519, FROST, SHA-512, Shamir secret sharing
- **Stated difference:** **none stated**

**ZK Arena / Log Forge**

- **Shared:** Baby-step giant-step, Pohlig–Hellman
- **Stated difference:** **none stated**

**Ratchet Wire / Encrochat**

- **Shared:** AES, AES-GCM, Diffie-Hellman, Double Ratchet, HKDF, SHA-256, X25519
- **Stated difference:** ratchet-wire demonstrates the Double Ratchet working as designed; encrochat reconstructs the 2020 Encrochat takedown, where the same construction was never broken and the endpoint was compromised instead

**Babel Hash / Hash Zoo**

- **Shared:** BLAKE3, SHA-256, SHA-3
- **Stated difference:** Both teach SHA-256/SHA3-256/BLAKE3, avalanche and real length-extension, so substantial overlap remains. Choose Babel Hash for the attack-to-defense sequence: sweep secret-length guesses, then test HMAC-SHA256 against the same attack. Choose Hash Zoo for construction inspection: examine SHA-256 padding and the SHA-3 rate/capacity split beside the Merkle-Damgard, sponge and tree views. Portfolio membership is not the distinction.

**STARK Tower / Polynomial Forge**

- **Shared:** FRI, Merkle tree, SHA-256
- **Stated difference:** stark-tower runs a whole STARK, prover and verifier, catching a cheating prover through a FRI low-degree test; polynomial-forge opens the commitment layer underneath and compares KZG, IPA and FRI as schemes in their own right

**Format Ward / Regex Veil — FTE**

- **Shared:** AES, AES-CBC, FF1
- **Stated difference:** format-ward PRESERVES an existing format with FF1 and FF3-1, so ciphertext keeps the length and alphabet of the input; fte TRANSFORMS ciphertext into whatever language a regular expression defines, by ranking a DFA slice

**VSS Gate / Reshare Circle**

- **Shared:** Feldman VSS, Pedersen commitment, Shamir secret sharing
- **Stated difference:** vss-gate adds VERIFIABILITY to Shamir sharing at deal time, through Feldman and Pedersen commitments; reshare-circle leaves the dealing alone and refreshes shares over time, using HJKY proactive sharing against perpetual leakage

**Blind Hello / Blind Relay**

- **Shared:** DHKEM, HPKE
- **Stated difference:** **none stated**

- **Stated difference:** **none stated**

## Labs

243 labs. Implementation findings and source coverage are separate questions.

**N/A (7)** — source-reviewed labs that model an attack or
system but implement no named algorithm in this index. N/A is a reviewed
finding, not the automatic scanner's answer to a miss.

**UNKNOWN (0)** — every file this scanner reads was read and no algorithm was
derivable, with no source review resolving whether that is an intentional model or
a missed implementation. Do not treat this as N/A.

**NOT-SCANNED (0)** — the lab implements its cryptography in a language this
scanner does not read, so there is no finding either way. `could not look` is not
`nothing there`, and collapsing the two would publish "implements nothing" about source
nobody opened.

**Partially unread (8)** — some bundled source or binary remains opaque
to this index; the algorithm list is a floor rather than a total.

### Ablation Wire

[`crypto-lab-ablation-wire`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-ablation-wire/) · Layer Ablation · PROTOCOLS, ATTACKS, POST-QUANTUM

The 1942 Navajo code-talker stack rebuilt on modern primitives, with every layer independently switchable — turn one off and discover which was actually load-bearing.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** X-Wing KEM, AES-256-GCM, Transcript Binding, Rust/WASM — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** AES-GCM `codetalker-core/src/aead.rs:5`, ChaCha20-Poly1305 `codetalker-core/src/aead.rs:6`, Ed25519 `codetalker-core/src/identity.rs:172`, HKDF `codetalker-core/src/kdf.rs:4`, ML-DSA `codetalker-core/src/identity.rs:221`, ML-KEM `codetalker-core/src/kem.rs:253`, SHA-256 `codetalker-core/src/kdf.rs:5`, X25519 `codetalker-core/src/kem.rs:97`
- **Source review:** [24ae374e44bd](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-ablation-wire/commit/24ae374e44bdf11e99e55be3361d6f8c42758fb3) — Re-read the merged PR21 Rust core, WASM callers, threat model, vendored libcrux source/provenance, compiler controls and learner-facing limits. The eight primitive implementations remain. Secret-typed u8 values now propagate through the verification-only ML-KEM, SHA3/SHAKE and X-Wing paths, with declassification limited to reviewed public outputs and embedded public-key bytes; positive and negative compiler controls pass. Shipping APIs, malformed-input handling and normal builds remain intact. This establishes source-level secret classification only, not constant-time machine code or browser-JIT side-channel resistance. A5 remains explicitly OutOfScope, so the side-channel warning is not an executed attack demonstration. Preserve the executed known-plaintext/reused-nonce and active MITM exhibits.
- **References:** AES, ChaCha20, DHKEM, Diffie-Hellman, Double Ratchet, EC point arithmetic, Pairing, Poly1305, SHA-3, SHAKE
- **Attacks shown:** Discrete log `TEACHING.md:243`, Known-plaintext attack `README.md:298`, Man-in-the-middle `web/index.html:2493`, Nonce reuse `web/index.html:1344`
- **Standards body:** IETF, NIST
- **Implementation:** Rust crates / WASM
- **Exhibit map:** NOT REVIEWED — no source-backed panel inventory yet; inspect the current lab before ruling out a concept.

### Adaptor Gate

[`crypto-lab-adaptor-gate`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-adaptor-gate/) · Scriptless Scripts · SIGNATURES, PROTOCOLS

One click turns a pre-signature the real BIP-340 verifier rejects into a valid signature, then subtracts the two to read the secret back out — the fact that atomic swaps and PTLC routing are both built on.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** BIP-340, secp256k1, Atomic Swap, PTLC — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** Schnorr `src/crypto/attacks.ts:8`, secp256k1 `src/crypto/adaptor.ts:156`, SHA-256 `src/crypto/vectors.ts:23`
- **Source review:** [f838c41a6708](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-adaptor-gate/commit/f838c41a6708ee52e70e395f394c53b513d31558) — secp256k1 is added by review because the scanner now reads `import { schnorr } from '@noble/curves/secp256k1.js'` as a module path rather than an implementation, which is right in general and wrong here: src/crypto/secp.ts wraps that import into the lab's own point and scalar layer (N, G, mulG, mul, liftX, invModN) and src/crypto/adaptor.ts computes the adaptor construction on it directly. The anchor is the defining point addition, R + T, not the import. Adaptor layer is the lab's own code over @noble/curves point/scalar ops; the completed signature is verified by the library's unmodified BIP-340 verify. Ledgers and PTLC routing are modeled and labelled as such in-page; PTLC settlement is causal (each hop consumes the value extracted downstream), not precomputed.
- **References:** EC point arithmetic, ECDSA, FROST

- **Standards body:** NIST, SECG

  - **Compare receipt-first and early-basis schedules** (`basis-announcement-order`; comparison; simulation)
    - **Visible section:** WHEN ARE BASES ANNOUNCED?
    - **Learner action:** Choose Bob confirms receipt first or Alice reveals bases too early and compare the exact four-state enumeration under the specified Eve.
    - **Observed result:** With Eve permitted to store each qubit until an early basis announcement, the modeled Eve learns the sifted bits without induced QBER; receipt-first forces a basis choice before the announcement and reveals the usual full-intercept disturbance.
    - **Concepts taught:** BB84; authenticated public discussion; basis announcement timing; quantum memory attack model
    - **Limits:** This exact enumeration is for a deliberately specified attack and timing assumption, not a general proof that receipt-first alone secures QKD.
    - **Evidence:** [`index.html:433`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/index.html#L433), [`index.html:437`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/index.html#L437), [`src/main.ts:932`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/src/main.ts#L932), [`src/main.ts:942`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/src/main.ts#L942), [`src/teaching.ts:155`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/src/teaching.ts#L155)
  - **Try public reconciliation and conditional extraction** (`conditional-postprocessing`; interactive; real-operation)
    - **Visible section:** TRY PUBLIC POST-PROCESSING
    - **Learner action:** Supply a hypothetical conditional min-entropy lower bound after an accepted run and press Try post-processing.
    - **Observed result:** The teaching model publishes Hamming syndromes and a 16-bit verification tag, attempts one correction per seven-bit block, subtracts public leakage and a margin from the assumed entropy budget, then may apply a public-seeded Toeplitz extractor or output zero bits.
    - **Concepts taught:** information reconciliation; conditional min-entropy; privacy amplification; leftover hash lemma; Toeplitz hashing
    - **Limits:** The supplied entropy bound is not inferred from QBER. The model is not a finite-key QKD proof, and its extracted bits are not used for the main AES-256 key.
    - **Evidence:** [`index.html:421`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/index.html#L421), [`index.html:424`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/index.html#L424), [`index.html:427`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/index.html#L427), [`src/main.ts:907`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/src/main.ts#L907), [`src/main.ts:914`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/src/main.ts#L914), [`src/teaching.ts:35`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/src/teaching.ts#L35), [`src/teaching.ts:102`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/src/teaching.ts#L102)
  - **Estimate errors and decide whether to abort** (`error-threshold`; interactive; simulation)
    - **Visible section:** Step 4 — Error Estimation
    - **Learner action:** Adjust channel noise or the QBER threshold and repeat; inspect the sacrificed-bit error count and decision gauge.
    - **Observed result:** The run aborts at or above the chosen threshold and discards the key, including when noise alone causes excess disturbance; below it the demonstration continues.
    - **Concepts taught:** QBER; error estimation; abort threshold; noise versus eavesdropping
    - **Limits:** The threshold is a teaching control, not a derived security bound. Alice and Bob see disturbance, not its cause.
    - **Evidence:** [`index.html:162`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/index.html#L162), [`index.html:304`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/index.html#L304), [`src/main.ts:665`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/src/main.ts#L665), [`src/main.ts:676`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/src/main.ts#L676), [`src/main.ts:686`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/src/main.ts#L686), [`src/main.ts:735`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/src/main.ts#L735)
  - **Hash retained bits and try AES-GCM** (`hash-and-aead`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Step 6 — Encrypt with AES-256-GCM
    - **Learner action:** After an accepted simulated exchange, inspect Alice's and Bob's separately SHA-256-derived keys and encrypt a message using Alice's key.
    - **Observed result:** AES-GCM decryption with Bob's key succeeds when the retained bits agree and rejects when residual bit disagreements produce a different key.
    - **Concepts taught:** SHA-256; AES-256-GCM; key agreement; information reconciliation
    - **Limits:** The cryptographic hash and AEAD run for real on bits generated by a classical BB84 simulation; the main run omits reconciliation and privacy amplification. Hashing does not create secrecy or prove Eve's knowledge is small.
    - **Evidence:** [`index.html:172`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/index.html#L172), [`index.html:309`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/index.html#L309), [`index.html:312`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/index.html#L312), [`src/main.ts:746`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/src/main.ts#L746), [`src/main.ts:813`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/src/main.ts#L813), [`src/main.ts:902`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/src/main.ts#L902), [`src/encrypt.ts:1`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-bb84/blob/7c5f98a250a0bc2bc789cc21047a28170b242880/src/encrypt.ts#L1)

Existing full-round providers and SHA-256/SHA-512 call-site anchors 79/81 remain unchanged. The isolated JavaScript research backend computes SHA-256 compression over big-endian blocks with the standard IV, explicit step count, per-block feed-forward and no added padding. The supplied two-block messages reproduce the 36-step Table 2 value from the 9 September 2026 preprint; this is distinct from its semi-free-start appendix examples. Normal WebCrypto SHA-256 with message padding produces different digests. Independent Python and TypeScript checks reproduce the result, reject all 1,024 one-bit mutations and distinguish incorrect round/IV/padding interpretations. Common padding preserves the reduced-round collision but changes the reported chaining value. The 64-step engine matches independent noble SHA-256 at padding boundaries. Local checks passed 118 units, lint/build and 35 browser tests, with one existing intentional skip; deployment passed separately. The sole Python file is the fully reviewed independent CI verifier, not an opaque browser component. The fixture records mirror retrieval and PDF fingerprint. This verifies a supplied pair, not its search cost, a full-round break, conformance certification or constant-time behavior.

The key space is 16 bits plus 24 bits, validated as such, which is the 40 bits the attack exhibit is about. divide.ts recover() enumerates smaller-register seeds and returns counted candidates; verify.ts checks a candidate against continuation bytes the search never saw. Scope recorded with it: this is the textbook generator, and the source says so in its own extension note -- deployed CSS changes insertion positions, discards early bytes and has inverter modes, none of which are implemented here. - **Implements:** AES `src/crypto/cipher.ts:29`, AES-GCM `src/crypto/cipher.ts:38`, ChaCha20 `src/crypto/chacha20.ts:86`, SHA-256 `src/crypto/seeded.ts:66`
- **Source review:** [f995c87c1fe0](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-good-randomness/commit/f995c87c1fe074dc57ee61b44c4c6df47a03de58) — Read src/crypto/chacha20.ts, cipher.ts, pinned.ts and vectors.ts. ChaCha20 is HAND-ROLLED here rather than imported, because it is the teaching subject and a reader has to be able to open the file: the scanner anchored it at src/crypto/pinned.ts:18, which is that file's import line, so the pin moves it to the block function it actually implements. AES-GCM and SHA-256 come from crypto.subtle and their anchors are the real call sites. The lab's point is that a generator seeded from a guessable value produces guessable keys while every check on the page still reports success -- the key from a four-digit PIN is rebuilt by trying ten thousand seeds, which is counting rather than cryptanalysis.

### Hash Hunt

[`crypto-lab-hash-hunt`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-hash-hunt/) · Generic Hash Attacks · HASHING &amp; KDFS, ATTACKS

Find truncated-SHA-256 collisions, transfer a tag in an insecure hash-then-MAC construction, and measure chained-table tradeoffs and the limits of salt.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** Truncated SHA-256, Floyd Cycle Finding, Hellman / Rainbow Chains, HMAC-SHA-256 — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** Floyd cycle finding `src/attack/floyd.ts:2`, Hellman chains `src/attack/tmto/tables.ts:8`, HMAC `src/mac/hashAndMac.ts:2`, Rainbow chains `src/attack/tmto/tables.ts:8`, SHA-256 `src/hash/truncate.ts:3`
- **Source review:** [3c766455e051](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-hash-hunt/commit/3c766455e051b48adb6af5356cb81257770f4ab4) — Read exact MSB truncation, independent SHA checks, collision predecessor recovery, injective meaningful-letter mapping, platform HMAC sign/verify, endpoint chain regeneration and salts sampled after precomputation. The tag transfer attacks a deliberately collision-prone hash-then-MAC composition, not HMAC or full SHA-256. Hellman uses one reduction column per table; rainbow varies the column. Coverage sets and diagnostic traces are additional memory. Length extension is a neighboring topic, not an executed exhibit. All 21 units, eight browser claims, two accessibility views and eleven mutations passed; this pin only clarifies README scope and integration.
- **References:** Grover's algorithm, MD5, Merkle tree, SHA-1, bcrypt

### HTTPS Padlock

[`crypto-lab-https-padlock`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-https-padlock/) · What the Padlock Means · PROTOCOLS, SIGNATURES

Takes apart a certificate a real site presented, lets you break each of its four checks in turn, then shows a flawless certificate for a lookalike domain that passes every one. Reads captured certificates; it never connects to a site.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** X.509, ECDSA P-256, RFC 5280 Subset, ClientHello Bytes Only — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** ECDSA `src/pki/path.ts:86`, X25519 `src/tls/clienthello.ts:282`
- **Source review:** [f5d5b09b548b](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-https-padlock/commit/f5d5b09b548bcb2f67b133bd19044cc3fc577eaa) — Read src/pki/path.ts, parse.ts, assess.ts, break.ts and src/tls/clienthello.ts. The scanner found only X25519 in the ClientHello builder. The chain walk really does verify every signature: src/pki/path.ts:86 calls @peculiar/x509's verify with the parent's public key and the WebCrypto provider, over real DER TBS bytes, and the certificates this lab ships are ECDSA over P-256 and P-384 -- so ECDSA is pinned above. Scope that the card and chips are written to respect: the lab makes NO network connection and runs no handshake, so it never observes encryption; it reads certificates captured earlier. Its RFC 5280 path validation is a stated teaching subset, deliberately omitting revocation, name constraints, policy constraints and path length, so a chain this page accepts is not thereby a chain a browser would accept. The ClientHello is encoded byte for byte and never sent, and its X25519 private half is discarded unused -- which is why the chip is marked 'ClientHello Bytes Only' rather than claiming TLS 1.3. Trust terminates in the lab's own committed copy of a root list, not the reader's device trust store, and the page says so. Re-read current hostname.ts, original PKI path and ClientHello at this exact SHA after PR4/5. Authority ends before path/query/fragment userinfo; 68 unit, 63 verdict, 3 full-state accessibility checks and 24 live URL/SNI/reflow controls verify the bounded repair. ECDSA anchor and captured-certificate/offline/partial-validation limitations remain unchanged; this review does not assert a live TLS handshake. Re-read complete current path.ts and parse.ts, bounded assess/ClientHello callers, trust-anchor regression controls and PR7 at f5d5b09. Actual held subject/SPKI identity now terminates cross-signed paths; copied subject with a different key rejects, genuine same-key cross-signs remain valid and held/served date policy stays explicit. X5092 reflection initialization preserves real ECDSA verification. Existing ECDSA86/X25519 ClientHello282 anchors unchanged. This source review retains offline captured-certificate/partial RFC5280 limits and does not establish live TLS, full validation, revocation or constant-time behavior.
- **References:** ChaCha20, ChaCha20-Poly1305, ECDH, Encrypted Client Hello, P-256, P-384, Poly1305, RSA, SHA-256, SHA-384, TLS 1.3
- **Standards body:** IETF, NIST
- **Implementation:** WebCrypto
- **Exhibit map:** NOT REVIEWED — no source-backed panel inventory yet; inspect the current lab before ruling out a concept.

### McEliece Gate

[`crypto-lab-mceliece-gate`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-mceliece-gate/) · Post-Quantum KEM · POST-QUANTUM

Run a toy binary Goppa code and Patterson decoder, then visualize Classic McEliece’s 261,120-byte public key using simulated bytes. McEliece began as public-key encryption in 1978; the later KEM was not selected when NIST chose HQC in 2025.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** Toy Goppa Code, Simulated Key Sizes, Post-Quantum — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** AES `src/mceliece.ts:173`, AES-GCM `src/mceliece.ts:182`, SHA-256 `src/mceliece.ts:81`
- **Source review:** [3f4a0d6ad769](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-mceliece-gate/commit/3f4a0d6ad7697a9027f3c703dbcc935a08dd1e25) — Reviewed src/mceliece.ts, src/toy/goppa-code.ts, keysize and comparison modules, visible UI, README, LIMITATIONS and tests at this pin. The browser computes a genuine small GF(16) Goppa/Patterson teaching model and a toy brute-force syndrome decoder. Its published-size 261120-byte key visual is SHA-256-expanded simulated bytes, not a Classic McEliece public key; its encapsulation is not the submitted KEM API. Real WebCrypto AES-GCM protects the teaching message. Classic McEliece is a referenced later KEM, not an implemented primitive here. The 2026 structural key-recovery preprint and possible public-key-substitution MitM are research/deployment context, not attacks executed by this lab. Preserve actual toy brute force and real AES/SHA operations while excluding full Classic McEliece, key recovery and MitM implementation credits. The 1978 scheme was public-key encryption; CRYSTALS-Kyber was selected in 2022 and standardized as ML-KEM in 2024. NIST selected HQC rather than Classic McEliece in 2025.
- **References:** BIKE, Classic McEliece, Grover's algorithm, HQC, Information-set decoding, Isogeny walk, Kyber, LWE, ML-KEM, NTRU, RSA, Reed-Muller, Reed-Solomon
- **Attacks shown:** Brute force `src/toy/goppa-code.ts:347`
- **Standards body:** NIST
- **Implementation:** toy GF(16) Goppa/Patterson model, simulated published-size key bytes, WebCrypto AES-GCM
- **Exhibit map:** PARTIALLY REVIEWED — selected sections only; unmapped sections may teach other concepts. Source pin [3f4a0d6ad769](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-mceliece-gate/commit/3f4a0d6ad7697a9027f3c703dbcc935a08dd1e25) reviewed 2026-10-22; 2 mapped sections.
  - **Scramble a toy binary Goppa generator** (`scramble-generator`; comparison; real-operation)
    - **Visible section:** 1. Binary Goppa Codes and the McEliece Trapdoor
    - **Learner action:** Switch between Bob's structured generator G, the row-mixed S·G matrix, and the permuted public Gpub matrix.
    - **Observed result:** Displays the computed toy matrices and explanatory captions showing how obvious visual structure changes under row mixing and column permutation.
    - **Concepts taught:** binary Goppa code; Classic McEliece; generator matrix; row scrambling; column permutation; public-key structure; structural attack
    - **Limits:** A GF(16), n=16 toy visual; a random-looking matrix display does not establish indistinguishability or structural-attack resistance of real Classic McEliece keys.
    - **Evidence:** [`src/ui.ts:254`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-mceliece-gate/blob/3f4a0d6ad7697a9027f3c703dbcc935a08dd1e25/src/ui.ts#L254), [`src/ui.ts:301`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-mceliece-gate/blob/3f4a0d6ad7697a9027f3c703dbcc935a08dd1e25/src/ui.ts#L301), [`src/ui.ts:730`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-mceliece-gate/blob/3f4a0d6ad7697a9027f3c703dbcc935a08dd1e25/src/ui.ts#L730), [`src/ui.ts:758`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-mceliece-gate/blob/3f4a0d6ad7697a9027f3c703dbcc935a08dd1e25/src/ui.ts#L758), [`src/ui.ts:763`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-mceliece-gate/blob/3f4a0d6ad7697a9027f3c703dbcc935a08dd1e25/src/ui.ts#L763), [`src/toy/goppa-code.ts:211`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-mceliece-gate/blob/3f4a0d6ad7697a9027f3c703dbcc935a08dd1e25/src/toy/goppa-code.ts#L211)
  - **Toy Goppa encapsulation, Patterson decoding and tampering** (`toy-kem`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** 3. Encapsulation & Decapsulation (Live Toy KEM)
    - **Learner action:** Encapsulate, toggle ciphertext bits or exceed the correction radius, decapsulate with the trapdoor, and run the toy brute-force attacker comparison.
    - **Observed result:** Shows the ciphertext and error weight, Patterson decoding steps and success or failure, shared-secret agreement, and the toy attack's search result; successful decapsulation can key an AES-GCM message round-trip.
    - **Concepts taught:** binary Goppa code; Patterson decoder; syndrome; error correction radius; key encapsulation; brute-force syndrome decoding; AES-256-GCM
    - **Limits:** A n=16, t=2 teaching KEM with toy brute force, not the production Classic McEliece KEM, a practical attack on real parameters, or the 2026 structural preprint's recovery method.
    - **Evidence:** [`src/ui.ts:423`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-mceliece-gate/blob/3f4a0d6ad7697a9027f3c703dbcc935a08dd1e25/src/ui.ts#L423), [`src/ui.ts:851`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-mceliece-gate/blob/3f4a0d6ad7697a9027f3c703dbcc935a08dd1e25/src/ui.ts#L851), [`src/ui.ts:873`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-mceliece-gate/blob/3f4a0d6ad7697a9027f3c703dbcc935a08dd1e25/src/ui.ts#L873), [`src/ui.ts:898`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-mceliece-gate/blob/3f4a0d6ad7697a9027f3c703dbcc935a08dd1e25/src/ui.ts#L898), [`src/ui.ts:1002`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-mceliece-gate/blob/3f4a0d6ad7697a9027f3c703dbcc935a08dd1e25/src/ui.ts#L1002), [`src/ui.ts:1025`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-mceliece-gate/blob/3f4a0d6ad7697a9027f3c703dbcc935a08dd1e25/src/ui.ts#L1025), [`src/toy/goppa-code.ts:276`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-mceliece-gate/blob/3f4a0d6ad7697a9027f3c703dbcc935a08dd1e25/src/toy/goppa-code.ts#L276)

Predict a generator's next output: read a toy LCG off its own recurrence, recover Java's 48-bit state from two ints, then lift a 512-bit truncated LCG with lattice reduction.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** LCG, java.util.Random, Lattice Reduction, ChaCha20 — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** ChaCha20 `src/gen/chacha.ts:5`
- **References:** BBS signatures
- **Attacks shown:** Lattice reduction `src/main.ts:16`
- **Standards body:** IETF
- **Implementation:** @noble
- **Exhibit map:** NOT REVIEWED — no source-backed panel inventory yet; inspect the current lab before ruling out a concept.

### Noise to Numbers

[`crypto-lab-noise-to-numbers`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-noise-to-numbers/) · Entropy Assessment · RANDOMNESS

Compare pinned SP 800-90B and Theseus results on seven reproducible inputs, inspect variability across simulated runs, and challenge the IID assumption. Entropy belongs to the source, not a statistical score.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** SP 800-90B, Min-Entropy, Keccak-f[1600], Modelled Noise Source — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** Keccak `src/entropy/keccak.ts:49`, SHA-256 `src/entropy/counter-hash.ts:85`, SHA-3 `src/entropy/keccak.ts:227`
- **References:** CTR-DRBG, DSA, HMAC-DRBG, MD5, One-time pad, Toeplitz extractor, von Neumann extractor
- **Standards body:** NIST
- **Implementation:** WebCrypto
- **Exhibit map:** PARTIALLY REVIEWED — selected sections only; unmapped sections may teach other concepts. Source pin [f468565fbc65](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-noise-to-numbers/commit/f468565fbc6530fcd98508b2493370dfa61aa88a) reviewed 2026-10-22; 12 mapped sections.
  - **Pinned non-IID assessment** (`assessment`; comparison; real-values)
    - **Visible section:** Assessment: [selected sample]
    - **Learner action:** Select a shipped fixture and inspect the minimum, per-bit conversion, branch rule and individual non-IID estimators.
    - **Observed result:** Recorded native SP 800-90B assessment shows the binding estimator and distinctions among bits per sample and bits per bit; custom files show Not Run.
    - **Concepts taught:** SP 800-90B non-IID assessment; min-entropy estimators; H_original; H_bitstring; minimum rule; sample width
    - **Limits:** No browser estimator for changed/uploaded bytes; a figure applies only to its exact hashed fixture and recorded native run.
    - **Evidence:** [`src/ui/assessPanel.ts:52`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-noise-to-numbers/blob/f468565fbc6530fcd98508b2493370dfa61aa88a/src/ui/assessPanel.ts#L52), [`src/ui/assessPanel.ts:102`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-noise-to-numbers/blob/f468565fbc6530fcd98508b2493370dfa61aa88a/src/ui/assessPanel.ts#L102), [`src/ui/assessPanel.ts:105`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-noise-to-numbers/blob/f468565fbc6530fcd98508b2493370dfa61aa88a/src/ui/assessPanel.ts#L105), [`src/ui/assessPanel.ts:215`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-noise-to-numbers/blob/f468565fbc6530fcd98508b2493370dfa61aa88a/src/ui/assessPanel.ts#L215), [`src/ui/assessPanel.ts:327`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-noise-to-numbers/blob/f468565fbc6530fcd98508b2493370dfa61aa88a/src/ui/assessPanel.ts#L327)

### Nonce Collision

[`crypto-lab-nonce-collision`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-nonce-collision/) · Nonce Reuse · ATTACKS, ENCRYPTION

Compare nonce reuse in AES-CTR, AES-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305 with a separate AES-CBC predictable-IV chosen-plaintext exercise. Observe keystream reuse and authenticated-mode forgery under each stated condition.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, Forbidden Attack, Crib Dragging — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** AES `src/crypto/aes.ts:78`, AES-CBC `src/crypto/aes.ts:94`, AES-CTR `src/crypto/aes.ts:78`, AES-GCM `src/crypto/aes.ts:157`, ChaCha20 `src/crypto/chacha20.ts:44`, ChaCha20-Poly1305 `src/crypto/aead.ts:70`, GHASH `src/crypto/ghash-attack.ts:46`, Poly1305 `src/crypto/aead.ts:48`
- **References:** AES-SIV, ChaCha20-Poly1305
- **Attacks shown:** Birthday bound `src/crypto/nonce.ts:16`, Chosen-plaintext attack `src/main.ts:391`, IV reuse `src/main.ts:343`, Key recovery `src/crypto/poly1305.ts:117`, Nonce reuse `src/crypto/aes.ts:242`
- **Standards body:** IETF, NIST
- **Implementation:** WebCrypto
- **Exhibit map:** PARTIALLY REVIEWED — selected sections only; unmapped sections may teach other concepts. Source pin [67b5574673ca](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-nonce-collision/commit/67b5574673ca767f9ad4d594663665c6075b9ca4) reviewed 2026-10-22; 3 mapped sections.
  - **CBC: different IVs can still leak** (`cbc-predictable`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** CBC: different IVs can still leak
    - **Learner action:** Run the chosen-plaintext predictable-IV case against a control where plaintext is committed before a fresh IV is drawn.
    - **Observed result:** Observe identical first ciphertext blocks under distinct, predictable IVs when P2=P1 XOR IV1 XOR IV2, compared with the random-IV control.
    - **Concepts taught:** CBC IV unpredictability; chosen-plaintext attack; CBC first-block equality; IV versus nonce
    - **Limits:** Controlled first-block equality only; no AES key or unknown-plaintext recovery, and no claim of a CBC padding oracle.
    - **Evidence:** [`index.html:296`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-nonce-collision/blob/67b5574673ca767f9ad4d594663665c6075b9ca4/index.html#L296), [`index.html:298`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-nonce-collision/blob/67b5574673ca767f9ad4d594663665c6075b9ca4/index.html#L298), [`index.html:299`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-nonce-collision/blob/67b5574673ca767f9ad4d594663665c6075b9ca4/index.html#L299), [`index.html:301`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-nonce-collision/blob/67b5574673ca767f9ad4d594663665c6075b9ca4/index.html#L301), [`src/main.ts:665`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-nonce-collision/blob/67b5574673ca767f9ad4d594663665c6075b9ca4/src/main.ts#L665)
  - **Same mistake, four outcomes** (`outcomes`; comparison; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Same mistake, four outcomes
    - **Learner action:** Run fresh-versus-reused IV/nonce scenarios for AES-CTR, AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305 and AES-CBC.
    - **Observed result:** Read primitive return values separately from security verdicts and a running table of plaintext exposure, forgery and key recovery; CBC reuse reveals prefix equality while AEAD reuse enables nonce-specific forgery.
    - **Concepts taught:** mode-specific nonce misuse; AES-CTR; AES-GCM GHASH; ChaCha20-Poly1305; AES-CBC IV reuse; authenticated encryption
    - **Limits:** The scoreboard records the demonstrated scenario and explicitly does not claim recovery of the AES or ChaCha20 encryption key; CBC and CTR supply no authentication.

### Paillier Gate

[`crypto-lab-paillier-gate`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/) · Additive Homomorphic Encryption · HOMOMORPHIC, MPC & THRESHOLD

Paillier's additive homomorphic cryptosystem with encrypt/decrypt, tallying without decryption, and direct links to voting systems and GG20 threshold ECDSA.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** Paillier, Additive HE, Private Voting, Aggregation — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** HMAC `src/ballots.ts:46`, Paillier `src/aggregation.ts:1`, SHA-256 `src/ballots.ts:46`
- **References:** BFV, BGV, EC point arithmetic, ECDSA, ElGamal, Shamir secret sharing
- **Attacks shown:** Ciphertext malleability `src/main.ts:1285`, Discrete log `src/main.ts:144`, Factoring `src/factor.worker.ts:44`, Side-channel (unspecified) `README.md:36`
- **Standards body:** IETF, NIST
- **Implementation:** WebCrypto
- **Exhibit map:** PARTIALLY REVIEWED — selected sections only; unmapped sections may teach other concepts. Source pin [6d73ec5564b7](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/commit/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa) reviewed 2026-10-22; 6 mapped sections.
  - **Rewrite an encrypted ballot and compare MAC admission** (`ballot-malleability`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Rewriting a sealed ballot
    - **Learner action:** Seal a set of 0/1 ballots, select a ballot and a public-key vote boost, then forge and re-tally with the Encrypt-then-MAC check on or off.
    - **Observed result:** Without authentication the forged ciphertext changes the tally despite hiding the original vote; with the MAC check the altered ballot is rejected, and the page shows the effect of dropping it.
    - **Concepts taught:** Paillier malleability; ballot integrity; ciphertext authentication; Encrypt-then-MAC
    - **Limits:** This locally keyed MAC checks outsider tampering, not whether an authorized voter submitted a valid 0-or-1 plaintext; it is not a full election protocol.
    - **Evidence:** [`src/main.ts:349`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L349), [`src/main.ts:379`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L379), [`src/main.ts:1165`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L1165), [`src/main.ts:1215`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L1215), [`src/main.ts:1239`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L1239), [`src/main.ts:1272`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L1272)
  - **Encrypt, repeat and re-randomize a message** (`encrypt-decrypt-rerandomize`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Encrypt and decrypt
    - **Learner action:** Encrypt a number, encrypt it again with fresh randomness, decrypt the ciphertext, then re-randomize it using only the public key.
    - **Observed result:** Different ciphertexts can decrypt to the same number; the page shows the new ciphertext and the decryption of each stored example.
    - **Concepts taught:** Paillier encryption; probabilistic encryption; ciphertext re-randomization
    - **Limits:** The demonstration uses very small, insecure key sizes; a re-randomization can occasionally return an unchanged ciphertext when the fresh factor is one.
    - **Evidence:** [`src/main.ts:183`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L183), [`src/main.ts:765`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L765), [`src/main.ts:810`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L810), [`src/main.ts:825`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L825), [`src/main.ts:916`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L916)
  - **Factor the educational modulus** (`factor-key`; interactive; real-operation)
    - **Visible section:** Attack the key: factor N
    - **Learner action:** Press Factor N against the generated small modulus and watch a budgeted Pollard rho search.
    - **Observed result:** When factoring succeeds within the budget, the worker reports steps/time, rebuilds the private key and can decrypt a ciphertext made in the preceding section; larger attempts may give up.
    - **Concepts taught:** integer factorization; Pollard rho; Paillier key recovery; security parameter
    - **Limits:** Success is conditional on tiny educational keys and a fixed search budget; it is not a practical attack on properly sized Paillier.
    - **Evidence:** [`src/main.ts:142`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L142), [`src/main.ts:151`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L151), [`src/main.ts:1382`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L1382), [`src/main.ts:1435`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L1435), [`src/main.ts:1465`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L1465)
  - **Generate a Paillier keypair** (`generate-toy-keypair`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Generate a keypair
    - **Learner action:** Choose a 64–192-bit educational modulus size and generate a keypair in a worker; inspect N, g and the private parameters.
    - **Observed result:** The page computes primes and Paillier key material and displays the resulting modulus bit length, which can be one bit below the nominal selection.
    - **Concepts taught:** Paillier encryption; key generation; composite modulus; modulus size
    - **Limits:** These tiny sizes are deliberately factorable and unsuitable for deployment; the page does not model a hardened key generator.
    - **Evidence:** [`src/main.ts:80`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L80), [`src/main.ts:90`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L90), [`src/main.ts:686`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L686), [`src/keygen.worker.ts:1`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/keygen.worker.ts#L1)
  - **Multiply ciphertexts to add plaintexts** (`homomorphic-addition-overflow`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Homomorphic addition
    - **Learner action:** Encrypt two inputs or hand in earlier ciphertexts, multiply the ciphertexts modulo N², decrypt the product, and try the modulus-overflow preset.
    - **Observed result:** The product decrypts to (A+B) mod N; the page also actually decrypts a naive integer sum of ciphertexts to show it generally fails and exposes wraparound when A+B reaches N.
    - **Concepts taught:** additive homomorphism; ciphertext multiplication; modular wraparound; input bounds
    - **Limits:** The plain sum must be kept below N to represent the intended integer; Paillier alone does not authenticate ciphertexts.
    - **Evidence:** [`src/main.ts:257`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L257), [`src/main.ts:950`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L950), [`src/main.ts:975`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L975), [`src/main.ts:989`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L989), [`src/main.ts:1036`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L1036)
  - **Aggregate encrypted counts with public weights** (`weighted-aggregation`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Weighted aggregation
    - **Learner action:** Enter counts and optional weights, then aggregate encrypted counts and exponentiate ciphertexts by public weights.
    - **Observed result:** The page decrypts the encrypted sum and weighted sum and compares them with plaintext totals, showing each encrypted weighted contribution.
    - **Concepts taught:** private aggregation; Paillier additive homomorphism; scalar multiplication under encryption
    - **Limits:** The scenario uses one local decryption key and educational modulus sizes; it is not a distributed private analytics protocol.
    - **Evidence:** [`src/main.ts:312`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L312), [`src/main.ts:322`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L322), [`src/main.ts:1052`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L1052), [`src/main.ts:1062`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L1062), [`src/main.ts:1095`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-paillier-gate/blob/6d73ec5564b75e3a595a74a0623e0b60380f6dfa/src/main.ts#L1095)

Recover an AES-128 key byte from simulated power traces. Correlation and differential power analysis use real statistics on modeled leakage; the JavaScript AES is not constant-time. An idealized AES table cache-line observation leaves 16 candidates without measuring browser hardware leakage.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** CPA, DPA, AES-128, Hamming Weight — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** AES `src/aes/aes.ts:123`
- **Source review:** [c8635e31bbc5](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-power-trace/commit/c8635e31bbc5ec93f0617a3bf5ee3747a08c70f1) — Reviewed AES core, CPA/DPA code, leakage traces, Exhibit 8 cache model, UI, README and tests through this pin. CPA means correlation power analysis, not chosen-plaintext attack. Real AES block encryption is anchored at src/aes/aes.ts:123; browser power traces use its S-box intermediate, while the shipped JavaScript AES is not constant-time. The separate, idealized T-table exhibit uses a known plaintext byte and one 64-byte cache-line address observation to leave 16 possible key bytes versus 256 in an all-lines control. It neither measures browser cache timing nor recovers a full key. Fault injection is sibling context. Keep power analysis and bounded key-recovery credits; exclude chosen-plaintext, cache-timing, fault-injection and timing side-channel claims as executed attacks. Followup commits strengthen browser assertions and remove decorative aria-hidden attributes; AES and attack anchors remain unchanged.
- **References:** NTT, RSA, Shamir secret sharing
- **Attacks shown:** Key recovery `README.md:69`, Known-plaintext attack `src/ui/cache.ts:59`, Power analysis `src/attack/dpa.ts:112`, Side-channel (unspecified) `src/ui/ui.ts:70`
- **Standards body:** NIST
- **Implementation:** hand-rolled

- **References:** AES, Diffie-Hellman, ECDH, Ed25519, Kyber, RSA, Shor's algorithm

### PQXDH Wire

[`crypto-lab-pqxdh-wire`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-pqxdh-wire/) · Post-Quantum Key Agreement · KEY EXCHANGE, POST-QUANTUM

One ML-KEM secret added to the X3DH transcript is what survives a future curve break. The prekey signature and the ratchet after it are untouched, so Bob can still be impersonated with every check green.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** X25519, ML-KEM-1024, HKDF-SHA-512, Ed25519 — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** AES `src/crypto/aead.ts:20`, AES-GCM `src/crypto/aead.ts:20`, Diffie-Hellman `src/model/ratchet-step.ts:74`, Ed25519 `src/pqxdh/bundle.ts:1`, HKDF `src/model/ratchet-step.ts:11`, ML-KEM `src/pqxdh/alice.ts:2`, PQXDH `src/pqxdh/kdf.ts:6`, SHA-512 `src/model/ratchet-step.ts:3`, X25519 `src/model/quantum.ts:1`, X3DH `src/main.ts:17`
- **References:** Double Ratchet, EdDSA, Kyber, Shor's algorithm
- **Standards body:** IETF, NIST
- **Implementation:** WebCrypto
- **Exhibit map:** PARTIALLY REVIEWED — selected sections only; unmapped sections may teach other concepts. Source pin [d057c986bbb3](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-pqxdh-wire/commit/d057c986bbb35d4677af9e9b868d217f27445880) reviewed 2026-10-22; 5 mapped sections.
  - **Grant curve and lattice breaks to an adversary model** (`adversary-secret-grants`; interactive; simulation)
    - **Visible section:** Open the boxes the model grants
    - **Learner action:** Complete the handshake, grant the model all X25519 private keys with Curve break, then optionally grant it the ML-KEM secret with Lattice break.
    - **Observed result:** With only the curve grant, it recomputes four DH outputs but lacks the KEM secret and cannot rederive the session key; with both grants, it derives the same session key.
    - **Concepts taught:** PQXDH; post-quantum forward secrecy; hybrid key exchange; X25519 break model; ML-KEM break model; session-key reconstruction
    - **Limits:** The model directly hands private values to the adversary. It neither runs Shor's algorithm nor breaks ML-KEM, and does not prove the security of a deployed implementation.
    - **Evidence:** [`src/main.ts:140`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-pqxdh-wire/blob/d057c986bbb35d4677af9e9b868d217f27445880/src/main.ts#L140), [`src/main.ts:147`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-pqxdh-wire/blob/d057c986bbb35d4677af9e9b868d217f27445880/src/main.ts#L147), [`src/main.ts:153`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-pqxdh-wire/blob/d057c986bbb35d4677af9e9b868d217f27445880/src/main.ts#L153), [`src/main.ts:541`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-pqxdh-wire/blob/d057c986bbb35d4677af9e9b868d217f27445880/src/main.ts#L541), [`src/main.ts:544`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-pqxdh-wire/blob/d057c986bbb35d4677af9e9b868d217f27445880/src/main.ts#L544), [`src/main.ts:553`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-pqxdh-wire/blob/d057c986bbb35d4677af9e9b868d217f27445880/src/main.ts#L553), [`src/model/quantum.ts:30`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-pqxdh-wire/blob/d057c986bbb35d4677af9e9b868d217f27445880/src/model/quantum.ts#L30), [`src/model/quantum.ts:49`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-pqxdh-wire/blob/d057c986bbb35d4677af9e9b868d217f27445880/src/model/quantum.ts#L49)

### Prime Witness

[`crypto-lab-prime-witness`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-prime-witness/) · Primality Testing · RANDOMNESS, ATTACKS

Follow Miller–Rabin witnesses, count lying bases, defeat fixed-base lists, and measure real prime generation without mistaking probable primes for proofs.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** Miller–Rabin, Fermat Test, Carmichael Numbers, Prime Generation — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** Fermat primality test `src/primality/fermat.ts:2`, Miller–Rabin `src/primality/millerRabin.ts:11`
- **Source review:** [c85f91a26720](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-prime-witness/commit/c85f91a26720f4f2d63b8b4471720cfcce49bb25) — Read the six exhibits, independent sieve/trial-prime checks, fixed-base counterexamples, exhaustive liar counting and generation workers. These are primality tests, not primality proofs. FIPS 186-5 Table B.1 is an explicitly limited generation-shape experiment, not conformant RSA generation or a DRBG. Trial factorization supports Korselt classification and displayed factors; the lab does not teach a separate factoring attack. All 34 units, seven browser claims, two accessibility views and seven mutations passed at the prior code-identical build; this pin updates only integration documentation.
- **References:** RSA
- **Standards body:** —
- **Implementation:** local BigInt primality engines
- **Overlaps:** `crypto-lab-factor-forge` — Factor Forge attacks composite integers; Prime Witness tests candidate primes and distinguishes witnesses, probable primes and proofs.
- **Exhibit map:** NOT REVIEWED — no source-backed panel inventory yet; inspect the current lab before ruling out a concept.

### Privacy Pass

[`crypto-lab-privacy-pass`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-privacy-pass/) · Anonymous Tokens · PRIVACY, PROTOCOLS

A token proves the issuer authorised someone without anyone — issuer, origin, or the two colluding — learning who. Remove the client's blind and nothing on the wire changes; the guarantee is simply gone.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** VOPRF P-384, DLEQ Proof, RFC 9578, Hash-to-Curve — labels do not establish what any section runs.
- **Implements:** Hash-to-curve `src/oprf/voprf.ts:47`, OPRF `src/main.ts:3`, P-384 `src/oprf/voprf.ts:1`, Privacy Pass `src/main.ts:4`, SHA-256 `src/oprf/voprf.ts:25`, SHA-384 `src/oprf/voprf.ts:64`
- **References:** EC point arithmetic, OPAQUE, RSA
- **Standards body:** IETF, NIST
- **Implementation:** @noble
- **Exhibit map:** PARTIALLY REVIEWED — selected sections only; unmapped sections may teach other concepts. Source pin [6ffe92170897](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-privacy-pass/commit/6ffe92170897bda9c582b16ec8caa6343f1d935e) reviewed 2026-10-22; 4 mapped sections.
  - **Link otherwise valid tokens by per-client issuer keys** (`per-client-key`; comparison; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Experiment mode
    - **Learner action:** Choose BROKEN: per-client published key, select a roster size of two, three or four clients, issue and redeem their tokens, then link ledgers.
    - **Observed result:** Each client verifies a valid DLEQ proof under its own published key and redeems; the UI counts distinct key-ID buckets and draws one link per client partition.
    - **Concepts taught:** Privacy Pass; DLEQ proof scope; issuer key consistency; key partitioning; key identifiers; collusion; unlinkability
    - **Limits:** A fixed local roster of two to four synthetic clients; valid per-client proofs alone do not establish that all clients saw the same globally published key.

### Stego Suite

[`crypto-lab-stego-suite`](https://systemslibrarian.github.io/crypto-lab-stego-suite/) · Steganography · STEGANOGRAPHY

Compare LSB, DCT, and adaptive image hiding with chi-squared steganalysis. Optional AES-GCM passphrase encryption versions its KDF and warns when opening legacy images.

- **Card topics (discovery only):** LSB, DCT, Adaptive Embedding, Chi-Squared Steganalysis — labels do not establish what any section runs.

AES-GCM is real WebCrypto encryption; PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 derives its optional passphrase key. Encrypted packet mode 2 uses 600000 iterations; mode 1 keeps 120000 only for legacy decoding with a warning. Unknown modes reject, and old/new PNG browser tests cover compatibility; neither mode rescues weak passphrases from offline guessing. F5-inspired DCT and WOW-inspired adaptive placement are disclosed models, not complete named schemes. SPA in steganalysis discussion is not Simple Power Analysis, so preserve that removal.

  - **Texture-guided versus sequential image embedding** (`adaptive`; comparison; real-operation)
    - **Visible section:** Exhibit 5 — Adaptive Steganography (WOW-inspired)
    - **Learner action:** Compute the Sobel texture map, embed the same message by texture-ranked and sequential placement, then compare the carriers.
    - **Observed result:** Shows residual maps, mean texture and smooth-region fraction at embedding sites, and each carrier's chi-squared verdict.

The scanner anchored both at line 1, which is the IMPORT line in each file; the pins above move them to the operations, so the index points at work rather than at a dependency. The derived attack anchor 'Factoring@README.md:50' is prose in the README explaining why today's keys fall, not an attack this lab mounts. CORRECTED 2026-10-06: this note said it was not carried and it was -- `add` replaces anchors but does not drop a derived attack, which takes `remove`.   - **Corrupt Alice's ephemeral key on the wire** (`corrupt-ephemeral-key`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Break it yourself
    - **Learner action:** Flip a byte of the transmitted EK_A public key and follow Bob's derivation and initial-message decryption.
    - **Observed result:** The independently computed secrets diverge and AES-GCM authentication fails at Bob.
    - **Concepts taught:** X3DH; ephemeral Diffie-Hellman; key agreement failure; AEAD authentication
    - **Limits:** The initial-message demonstration omits X3DH's identity-key associated data, explicitly disclosed in src/ui.ts:628.
    - **Evidence:** [`src/ui.ts:202`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-x3dh-wire/blob/2d2d5b13bcb115b43a76feb4470a5ea1770bba62/src/ui.ts#L202), [`src/x3dh.ts:292`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-x3dh-wire/blob/2d2d5b13bcb115b43a76feb4470a5ea1770bba62/src/x3dh.ts#L292), [`src/x3dh.ts:309`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-x3dh-wire/blob/2d2d5b13bcb115b43a76feb4470a5ea1770bba62/src/x3dh.ts#L309), [`src/x3dh.ts:314`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-x3dh-wire/blob/2d2d5b13bcb115b43a76feb4470a5ea1770bba62/src/x3dh.ts#L314), [`src/ui.ts:624`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-x3dh-wire/blob/2d2d5b13bcb115b43a76feb4470a5ea1770bba62/src/ui.ts#L624)
  - **Drop the optional one-time prekey** (`optional-one-time-prekey`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Break it yourself
    - **Learner action:** Toggle off Bob's one-time prekey and examine the DH set and status strip.
    - **Observed result:** The fourth DH term is omitted, while Alice and Bob can still derive a matching shared secret.
    - **Concepts taught:** X3DH; one-time prekeys; DH4; asynchronous key agreement; forward secrecy
    - **Limits:** This teaching contrast does not constitute a forward-secrecy proof.
    - **Evidence:** [`src/ui.ts:201`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-x3dh-wire/blob/2d2d5b13bcb115b43a76feb4470a5ea1770bba62/src/ui.ts#L201), [`src/ui.ts:227`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-x3dh-wire/blob/2d2d5b13bcb115b43a76feb4470a5ea1770bba62/src/ui.ts#L227), [`src/x3dh.ts:275`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-x3dh-wire/blob/2d2d5b13bcb115b43a76feb4470a5ea1770bba62/src/x3dh.ts#L275), [`src/x3dh.ts:300`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-x3dh-wire/blob/2d2d5b13bcb115b43a76feb4470a5ea1770bba62/src/x3dh.ts#L300)
  - **Replace the whole prekey bundle** (`replace-whole-bundle`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Break it yourself
    - **Learner action:** Offer a different identity key and its correctly signed prekey, then compare the offered fingerprint with a previously trusted Bob fingerprint.
    - **Observed result:** The signature can remain valid while the identity pin mismatches. The deliberately unpinned continuation lets the attacker derive the same session key and decrypt the first message.
    - **Concepts taught:** X3DH; identity verification; out-of-band key comparison; active impersonation; bundle substitution
    - **Limits:** The trusted fingerprint is a teaching fixture; real users must authenticate identities independently. The unpinned continuation demonstrates the failure and is not a secure protocol path.
    - **Evidence:** [`src/ui.ts:200`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-x3dh-wire/blob/2d2d5b13bcb115b43a76feb4470a5ea1770bba62/src/ui.ts#L200), [`src/ui.ts:253`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-x3dh-wire/blob/2d2d5b13bcb115b43a76feb4470a5ea1770bba62/src/ui.ts#L253), [`src/x3dh.ts:251`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-x3dh-wire/blob/2d2d5b13bcb115b43a76feb4470a5ea1770bba62/src/x3dh.ts#L251), [`src/x3dh.ts:302`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-x3dh-wire/blob/2d2d5b13bcb115b43a76feb4470a5ea1770bba62/src/x3dh.ts#L302), [`src/x3dh.ts:323`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-x3dh-wire/blob/2d2d5b13bcb115b43a76feb4470a5ea1770bba62/src/x3dh.ts#L323), [`src/ui.ts:625`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-x3dh-wire/blob/2d2d5b13bcb115b43a76feb4470a5ea1770bba62/src/ui.ts#L625)
  - **Tamper the signed prekey signature** (`tamper-signed-prekey`; interactive; real-crypto)
    - **Visible section:** Break it yourself
    - **Learner action:** Flip the SPK signature byte or substitute an attacker-signed SPK while Bob's identity key remains in the bundle.
    - **Observed result:** XEdDSA verification fails and the X3DH handshake aborts before deriving a shared secret or sending a message.
    - **Concepts taught:** X3DH; signed prekeys; XEdDSA; prekey-bundle substitution; signature verification
    - **Evidence:** [`src/ui.ts:198`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-x3dh-wire/blob/2d2d5b13bcb115b43a76feb4470a5ea1770bba62/src/ui.ts#L198), [`src/ui.ts:199`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-x3dh-wire/blob/2d2d5b13bcb115b43a76feb4470a5ea1770bba62/src/ui.ts#L199), [`src/x3dh.ts:273`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-x3dh-wire/blob/2d2d5b13bcb115b43a76feb4470a5ea1770bba62/src/x3dh.ts#L273), [`src/x3dh.ts:279`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-x3dh-wire/blob/2d2d5b13bcb115b43a76feb4470a5ea1770bba62/src/x3dh.ts#L279), [`src/ui.ts:210`](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab-x3dh-wire/blob/2d2d5b13bcb115b43a76feb4470a5ea1770bba62/src/ui.ts#L210)
